title: Group OSCORE roster auth is not bound to the group
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Membership Synchronization: GET /groups/{id}/members is OSCORE-protected with the group context for that group. Full membership is not broadcast.

_roster_view_authorized (410-415) returns True if _group_oscore_identity(request) is not None. _group_oscore_identity (73-85) returns the first bound value that _is_group_oscore_context accepts. That classifier (53-59) is only:
- value == \"group\", or
- external_aad_is_group, or
- is_signing

The returned identity is never compared to item[\"id\"], item[\"key_id\"], or an OSCORE id_context. Possessing any RFC 9203 group context (group A) authorizes GET /groups/{B} (full document with members/admins) and GET /groups/{B}/members.

Pairwise affiliation is correctly scoped via requester_role(item[\"id\"], peer). Group-mode is a boolean. test_groups_item.py group_ctx_request uses a generic _GroupOscoreContext and does not create a second group.

This is not worker6-yuvj (unprotected GET). Current code already gates on some group context; it does not gate on the right one.
acceptance_criteria: GET /groups/{id} roster fields and GET /groups/{id}/members MUST require a group OSCORE context for that group (id_context/key_id/group_id match) or a pairwise identity with requester_role for that id. A group context for group A against group B returns 4.03 with no members/admins. Tests cover two encrypted groups and a swapped group context.
close_reason: Roster disclosure now requires a live RFC 9203 context bound to the exact encrypted group and current key epoch via id_context, group_id plus key_epoch, or key_id; affiliated pairwise identities remain group-scoped. Cross-group, unbound, mixed, and stale contexts return 4.03 with no roster. Full group/OSCORE tests, Ruff, and focused mypy passed.
